assessment.name: Year 8 Maths Summer assessment
assessment.sections: Date to be confirmed. From the school Year 8 Maths Revision List, Summer section.
assessment.weighting: Perimeter and area, circles, and 3D shapes (volume and surface area). Averages, scatter graphs and two way tables are taught in Summer but assessed in Year 9, so they are not in this deck. Sparx codes on each card lead to the videos.
assessment.equipment: Pen, pencil, ruler, compasses, calculator with a π button

mock.note: 25 questions over the units you have studied. Write the formula before you put numbers in.

cards.title: Perimeter
cards.question: How do you find the perimeter of shapes, including compound shapes? (Sparx videos: M920, M635, M690)
points: Perimeter is the total distance around the outside of a shape. Add every side.
On a grid, count the unit lengths along each edge.
For an L shaped (compound) shape, find missing sides first: opposite sides of the whole shape must match.
Give the answer with length units, such as cm or m.
cards.watch_out: Check you have a length for every side before adding. Missing sides are the most common error.
cards.hook: Perimeter: the fence around the field.
cards.grade9: Mark each side as you add it so none is counted twice or missed.

cards.title: Area of rectangles, parallelograms and triangles
cards.question: How do you find the area of rectangles, parallelograms and triangles? (Sparx videos: M390, M900, M610)
points: Rectangle: length × width. Square: side × side.
Parallelogram: base × perpendicular height.
Triangle: ½ × base × perpendicular height, because a triangle is half a parallelogram.
On a grid, count whole squares and pair up the half squares.
cards.watch_out: Use the perpendicular (straight up) height, not the sloping side.
cards.hook: Area is the carpet; perimeter is the fence.
cards.grade9: Explain why the triangle formula halves the parallelogram formula, using a diagram.

cards.title: Area of a trapezium
cards.question: How do you find the area of a trapezium? (Sparx video: M705)
points: Area = ½ × (a + b) × h, where a and b are the parallel sides and h is the perpendicular height.
Add the parallel sides, halve, then multiply by the height.
Parallel sides 4 cm and 10 cm, height 5 cm: ½ × 14 × 5 = 35 cm².
cards.watch_out: Only the two parallel sides go in the brackets, not the slanted sides.
cards.hook: Half the sum of the parallel sides, times the distance between them.
cards.grade9: Rearrange to find a missing side when you know the area.

cards.title: Compound shapes and coverage problems
cards.question: How do you find the area of compound shapes and solve coverage problems? (Sparx videos: M269, M996, M303)
points: Split a compound shape into rectangles and triangles, find each area, then add (or subtract a cut out part).
Coverage: area to cover ÷ area one item covers. A 10 m² wall with tins that cover 3 m² needs 10 ÷ 3 = 3.33, so 4 tins.
Round up for coverage: you cannot buy part of a tin.
Then work out the cost: number of items × price.
cards.watch_out: Rounding 3.33 down to 3 tins leaves part of the wall unpainted. Always round up.
cards.grade9: Show each area clearly labelled so the examiner can follow your method.

cards.title: Converting units of area
cards.question: How do you convert between units of area? (Sparx video: M728)
points: 1 cm = 10 mm, so 1 cm² = 10 × 10 = 100 mm².
Big unit to small unit: multiply. Small unit to big unit: divide.
cards.watch_out: 1 m² is not 100 cm². Square the length conversion factor.
cards.grade9: Convert lengths before working out the area if the sides are in different units.

cards.title: Parts of a circle
cards.question: What are the parts of a circle called? (Sparx video: M595)
points: Radius: centre to the edge. Diameter: edge to edge through the centre (2 × radius).
Circumference: the distance around the circle.
Chord: a straight line joining two points on the circle. Tangent: a straight line that touches the circle at one point.
Arc: part of the circumference. Sector: a slice made by two radii (like pizza). Segment: the part cut off by a chord.
cards.watch_out: Sector and segment are often confused: a sector has two radii, a segment has a chord.
cards.hook: Sector = slice of pizza; segment = slice of orange cut off by a chord.
cards.grade9: Label a diagram from memory, then check every part.

cards.title: Circumference and area of a circle
cards.question: How do you find the circumference and area of a circle? (Sparx videos: M169, M231)
points: Circumference = π × diameter, or 2 × π × radius.
Area = π × radius². Square the radius first.
Radius 5 cm: circumference = 2 × π × 5 = 31.4 cm; area = π × 25 = 78.5 cm² (1 dp).
If you are given the diameter, halve it to get the radius for the area.
cards.watch_out: π × r² is not (π × r)². Square only the radius.
cards.hook: Cherry pie delicious (C = πd). Apple pies are too (A = πr²).
cards.grade9: Leave answers in terms of π when asked for an exact answer, such as 25π cm².

cards.title: Area of a sector
cards.question: How do you find the area of a sector? (Sparx video: M430)
points: A sector is a fraction of a circle: angle ÷ 360.
Sector area = (angle ÷ 360) × π × r².
Quarter circle, radius 6 cm: 90 ÷ 360 × π × 36 = 28.3 cm² (1 dp).
A semicircle is a sector with an angle of 180°.
cards.watch_out: Use the angle of the sector itself, not the angle of the part left over.
cards.grade9: Work out a perimeter of a sector too: two radii plus the arc length (angle ÷ 360 × 2πr).

cards.title: Properties of 3D shapes and nets
cards.question: What are faces, edges and vertices, and what is a net? (Sparx videos: M767, M518)
points: Faces are flat surfaces, edges are where faces meet, vertices are corners.
Cube or cuboid: 6 faces, 12 edges, 8 vertices. Triangular prism: 5 faces, 9 edges, 6 vertices.
Square based pyramid: 5 faces, 8 edges, 5 vertices.
A net is a 2D shape that folds up to make a 3D shape. A cube has 11 different nets.
cards.watch_out: Not every arrangement of 6 squares folds into a cube. Imagine folding to check no faces overlap.
cards.hook: Faces are flat, edges are lines, vertices are points.
cards.grade9: Use a net to find surface area: the area of the net is the surface area of the shape.

cards.title: Volume of cuboids and prisms
cards.question: How do you find the volume of cuboids and prisms? (Sparx videos: M765, M722)
points: Volume of a cuboid = length × width × height. 4 cm × 3 cm × 2 cm = 24 cm³.
A prism has the same cross section all the way through.
Volume of a prism = area of cross section × length.
Triangular prism with triangle base 6 cm, height 4 cm and length 10 cm: ½ × 6 × 4 = 12, then 12 × 10 = 120 cm³.
cards.watch_out: Volume is in cubic units (cm³), area in square units (cm²).
cards.grade9: Find a missing length by dividing the volume by the area of the cross section.

cards.title: Volume of a cylinder
cards.question: How do you find the volume of a cylinder? (Sparx video: M697)
points: A cylinder is a prism with a circle as its cross section.
Volume = π × r² × h.
Radius 3 cm, height 10 cm: π × 9 × 10 = 282.7 cm³ (1 dp).
Halve the diameter first if you are given it.
cards.watch_out: Square the radius only, then multiply by the height.
cards.grade9: Compare capacities of two tins by working out both volumes and stating which holds more.

cards.title: Surface area of cuboids, prisms and cylinders
cards.question: How do you find surface area? (Sparx videos: M534, M661, M936)
points: Surface area is the total area of all the faces. Units are square, such as cm².
Cuboid: 2(lw + lh + wh). A 4 × 3 × 2 cuboid: 2(12 + 8 + 6) = 52 cm².
Prism: add the areas of every face. Sketch the net to make sure none is missed.
Cylinder: two circles plus the curved surface. 2πr² + 2πrh. Radius 3 cm, height 10 cm: 18π + 60π = 78π = 245.0 cm².
cards.watch_out: Do not mix up volume (inside space, cm³) with surface area (outside covering, cm²).
cards.hook: Curved surface unrolls into a rectangle: circumference × height.
cards.grade9: List every face with its area in a table before adding, so you can check the count of faces.

cards.title: Summer formulas to remember
cards.question: Can you recall each Summer formula?
points: Rectangle lw; parallelogram bh; triangle ½bh; trapezium ½(a + b)h.
Circle: C = πd = 2πr; A = πr²; sector = (angle ÷ 360) × πr².
Volume of a prism = cross section area × length; cylinder πr²h.
Surface area = total area of all faces; cylinder 2πr² + 2πrh.
1 m² = 10 000 cm²; 1 cm² = 100 mm².
cards.watch_out: Write the formula first, then substitute, then give the answer with the right units.
cards.grade9: Check units every time: lengths cm, areas cm², volumes cm³.

written.q: A wall is 4 m wide and 2.5 m tall. One tin of paint covers 3 m² and costs £12. How much will it cost to paint the wall?
A circular pond has a diameter of 8 m. Work out its area to 1 decimal place.
A cylinder has radius 3 cm and height 10 cm. Work out its volume and its surface area to 1 decimal place.

exam_tips.timing: Spend about 1 minute per mark. Write the formula before every calculation.
section_a: Check whether you are given the radius or the diameter.
Use the π button on the calculator, not 3.14, unless told to.
Give the units every time: cm, cm² or cm³.
section_b: Show the formula, the numbers and the answer.
For compound shapes, label each part and its area.
grade9: Sketch the net of a 3D shape before finding its surface area, so no face is missed.
Give exact answers in terms of π when the question asks for exact.
Round up in coverage problems and say why.
week: Most days, 10 to 15 minutes: press Start today (due cards, the new batch, then a short quiz).
Once a week, 10 minutes: measure a room or a tin at home and work out its area or volume with units. Then one Written practice question with every step shown.
Once a week: a quiz on the Quiz tab that mixes older units with this week's, so earlier topics stay in.
Fix one mistake: rewrite one wrong answer or one watch out from memory, then check it against the card.

vocab.meaning: The total distance around the outside of a shape
vocab.example: The perimeter of the garden is 24 m.

vocab.meaning: The amount of flat space inside a shape
vocab.example: The area of the rug is 6 m².

vocab.meaning: The distance from the centre of a circle to its edge
vocab.example: The radius of the wheel is 30 cm.
The circumference of the plate is 75 cm.

vocab.meaning: A slice of a circle between two radii
vocab.example: Each sector of the pie chart is a different colour.

vocab.meaning: A 3D shape with the same cross section all the way through
vocab.example: A tent shaped box is a triangular prism.

vocab.meaning: The amount of space inside a 3D shape
vocab.example: The volume of the box is 24 cm³.

vocab.meaning: A corner of a shape (plural: vertices)
vocab.example: Each vertex of a cube joins three edges.
